text: Something sophisticated is advanced and cleverly complicated, with many carefully designed parts working together instead of one simple part doing one simple job. Here the brands built more sophisticated movements: watch mechanisms with more pieces, doing more than just showing the hours and minutes. Used about a person, the word means worldly and refined, which is probably the meaning you already know.

Subsequent means coming after, later in time than the thing just mentioned. It is the word writers use when they do not want to list the years, games or chapters one by one. The pandemic and the subsequent years means the pandemic plus the stretch of years that followed it.

Something deliberate is done on purpose, planned and intended rather than an accident or a side effect. Rolex says the shortage of its watches is not deliberate policy: it claims it does not hold watches back on purpose, it just makes them slowly and carefully. Careful with the sound of it, because the verb deliberate, meaning to think something over, ends in a different way.

In business writing volume means the number of things, not loudness. The volume of exports is how many watches left Switzerland, which is a completely different number from how much money they sold for. That is the whole puzzle of this article: the volume fell by half while the money went up.

Value here means a total in money, not how useful or important something is. When the article says the volume of exports tumbled but their value kept rising, it means fewer watches were shipped and yet buyers paid more in total. Writers often pair volume and value like this to show two sides of the same trade.

A listed company is one whose shares are bought and sold on a stock exchange, so anyone can own a piece of it and its price is public every day. Swatch is the largest listed Swiss watchmaker, which is why the article can quote its share price. The other big watch brands are not listed, so no one outside them sees those numbers.

A privately owned company has no shares on a stock exchange. It belongs to a family, a small group of owners or a foundation, and it does not have to publish its profits or answer to outside shareholders. Most of the top Swiss watch brands are privately owned, which lets them stay quiet about their numbers and plan over many years.

A firm is simply a company or business. It has nothing to do with firm meaning hard or steady. Norqain is called a Swiss family-owned firm, and later the firm made only 300 of them means that company did.

Captured here means took or won, not caught something alive. Five brands captured 60% of revenue means those five collected 60% of all the money paid for Swiss watches. Business writers also say a company captured a market or captured share.

In this sentence bar means except. All bar Omega have been gaining share tells you that four of the five big brands grew their slice and Omega did not. It is a short, slightly formal word you meet often in British writing, and it has nothing to do with a bar you sit at.

Cartier apart means except for Cartier. English lets you put apart after a word to mean leaving that one out, so the sentence says every big luxury brand other than Cartier is privately owned. Watch for it at the start of a sentence, because it is easy to read straight past.

A watch movement is the engine inside the case: the parts that keep the hands turning at the right speed. A mechanical movement uses a wound spring and dozens of tiny gears. A quartz movement uses a battery and a vibrating crystal instead, which is cheaper to build and keeps better time.

Mechanical means working by moving physical parts, with no electricity involved. A mechanical watch runs on a coiled spring that slowly uncoils and pushes a train of small gears, which is where the ticking comes from. A mechanical pencil, a mechanical lock and a wind-up toy all work on the same idea.

Quartz is a hard, clear crystal found in rock, and a thin sliver of it vibrates at a very steady rate when electricity passes through. A quartz watch counts those vibrations, which is why it needs a battery and keeps better time than a spring can. Quartz watches are also cheap to make, so they were the ones smart watches took customers from.

To consolidate a market is for a few big players to end up with most of it, as smaller ones shrink or disappear. The deck says Rolex and Patek Philippe are consolidating the market: there are still hundreds of Swiss brands, but the money is gathering into fewer and fewer hands. The everyday meaning is to bring separate things together into one stronger whole.

The dial of a watch is its face, the flat surface the hands sweep across and the part you read the time from. Norqain cut one dial out of an iron meteorite, which is why that watch is unusual. The word has nothing to do with dialling a phone here.

To launch a product is to put it on sale for the first time, with announcements and attention. When the pair launched Royal Pop, they released a new watch and buyers queued for it. The same word covers launching a rocket, a ship or a video game.

In business writing a group means one big parent company and all the smaller brands it owns. Swatch Group owns Swatch, Omega and other labels, so pushed the group back into profit means the whole family of brands, not one watch line. Companies report their results for the group as a single total.

A company's results are the figures it publishes about how it did over a few months or a year, especially sales and profit. Saying Omega and the other fancy brands had mixed results means some of those numbers were good and some were poor. It is a regular thing companies must announce, not a one-off.

Mixed here means partly good and partly bad, with no clear overall direction. Results have been mixed is the polite way of saying some brands grew and others slipped. You will meet it in reviews and reports whenever the news does not point one way.

To channel money is to send it along a set path towards one purpose, the way a channel guides water. The Rolex foundation channels profits back into research and development, meaning the money does not go to owners but is directed into improving the watches. Nothing is being decided by the channel itself; people set the path.

A site is a piece of land with a building or works on it, here a factory location. Swatch has not closed any of those sites means all 150 factory locations are still standing and still costing money, even though it now makes far fewer watches. Think building site or construction site, not a website.

To tumble is to fall suddenly and steeply, the way a gymnast or a rockslide tumbles down. Writers use it for numbers that drop fast, so the volume of exports has tumbled means the count of watches shipped fell sharply. It is stronger than slipped and less formal than declined.

To plunge is to drop very fast and very far, like diving straight into deep water. Net profit plunged by almost 90% means Swatch kept barely a tenth of the profit it had made the year before. Plunged is about the strongest fall word in the business pages.

Bloated means swollen far beyond the right size, and about a company it means carrying far more buildings, staff or machinery than the work needs. A bloated production infrastructure is Swatch keeping 150 factories to make a quarter of the watches it used to. It is a criticism, never a compliment.

Swanky means expensive and showy in a stylish way, the sort of thing meant to be noticed. The headline says the Swiss watch industry is getting swankier: fewer watches, but grander and pricier ones. It is a playful, informal word, close to posh or fancy.

To queue is to wait in a line, one person behind another. Buyers all over the world queued for hours means people stood in line outside shops to buy the new watch. Queue is the usual British word where American English says line up.

Wares are the goods someone has for sale. The scarcity of its wares means there are not enough Rolex watches to go round. It is an old-fashioned word, and you mostly meet it now in phrases like peddling his wares.

Something scarce is in short supply, so there is not enough of it for everyone who wants it. Rolex says the scarcity of its watches is a side effect of careful making, not a plan. The last line of the article plays on the word: it is time that is scarce, because hand-building a watch takes so long.

Philanthropic means giving money away to help people, usually through gifts to causes, schools or hospitals. The Rolex foundation supports philanthropic causes in Geneva, so some of the profit from the watches goes to local good works. A person who does this on a large scale is called a philanthropist.

To differentiate yourself is to make yourself clearly different from your rivals, so buyers can tell you apart. Watch brands did it with new materials and more complicated movements, like a dial cut from a meteorite. In science class the same word means to tell two things apart.

Upmarket means aimed at richer buyers, with higher prices and fancier goods. The upmarket switch is the whole industry moving towards expensive watches. Its opposite, downmarket, means cheaper and aimed at everybody.

Infrastructure is the large, permanent equipment a business or country needs in order to work at all: factories, machines, roads, power lines, pipes. Swatch's production infrastructure is its buildings and watchmaking machinery. The point here is that infrastructure costs money even when it is standing idle.

A meteorite is a lump of rock or metal from space that has fallen through the atmosphere and landed on Earth. Most of the metal ones are mainly iron, formed inside long-broken-up bodies in the solar system. Norqain cut one of its watch dials from an iron meteorite found in Sweden, which is a real piece of space rock on someone's wrist.

Revenue is all the money a company takes in from selling things, before any costs are taken out. Rolex brought in revenue of more than SFr11bn, which is what buyers paid in total, not what Rolex kept. What is left after wages, parts and rent is profit, a much smaller number.

Net profit is what a company has left after every cost is paid, including wages, materials, rent and tax. It is the real bottom line, much smaller than revenue. Swatch's net profit plunging by almost 90% means it kept only a sliver of what it kept the year before, even though it still sold millions of watches.

A share is one small piece of ownership in a listed company, and the share price is what one piece costs on the stock exchange today. It moves up and down with what buyers think the company is worth. Swatch's share price being 40% lower than in early 2023 means investors now think the whole company is worth far less.

To gain share is to take a bigger slice of a market than you had before. It does not mean selling more: a brand can gain share in a year when its own sales fall, as long as its rivals fall faster. In a shrinking industry that is exactly how five brands ended up with 60% of the money.

Exports are goods sold out of the country that made them. Swiss watch exports make up 95% of all Swiss watch sales, so almost every watch made there is bought by someone abroad. Goods coming the other way, into a country, are imports.

The retail price is what an ordinary customer pays in a shop, as opposed to the lower wholesale price a shop pays the maker. The average retail price of a Rolex is SFr14,000, about 16,800 US dollars. Retail means selling to the public in small amounts.

An authorised dealer is a shop a brand has officially approved to sell its products, often the only kind of shop allowed to. Rolex decides which dealers may sell its watches and how many each one gets, which is why you cannot simply walk in and buy the model on display. The brand keeps control of the price and the experience that way.

A year-on-year figure compares a month or quarter with the very same stretch twelve months earlier, instead of with the month just gone. It is used because many businesses are naturally busier at some times of year. August being 9.1% higher year-on-year means it beat the previous August, not July.

As many means the same number as the one just mentioned, so the fourth rise in as many months is the fourth rise in four months, one every month. English uses this to avoid repeating a number. You will see it as three goals in as many games or two wins in as many weeks.

Premiumisation is a made-up business word for a whole industry drifting towards dearer, fancier versions of the same product. In watches it means fewer cheap models and more expensive ones. The article puts it in quote marks the first time because it is industry jargon rather than normal English.

A charitable trust is a legal arrangement that holds money or property and must use it for good causes rather than for an owner's own benefit. Rolex is owned by one, set up in 1945 by a founder with no children, so the profits flow into research and into causes in Geneva instead of to a family. Nobody can sell Rolex, because a trust is not for sale.

Research and development, usually shortened to R&D, is the work a company does to invent and improve its products rather than to make and sell them today. It costs money now and only pays off later. Rolex's owner channels profits back into R&D, which is how a company funds better materials and new designs.

Switzerland is divided into 26 cantons, which are like states or provinces with a lot of power of their own, including their own taxes and schools. Geneva is one of them, and it is the canton Rolex is based in. Knowing the word helps whenever you read about Swiss politics.

The chief executive, often called the CEO, is the person in charge of running a company day to day and answering for its decisions. Ben Küffer is chief executive of Norqain. Quoting one is a standard way for an article to get the view from inside an industry.

SFr stands for Swiss francs, the money used in Switzerland, which is worth a little more than a US dollar. SFr14,000 is about 16,800 dollars. When you see bn after a figure it means billion, so SFr11bn is eleven billion francs.

A composite is a material made by combining two different materials so the mixture is better than either alone. Carbon fibre is hair-thin strands of carbon, and setting them in hardened plastic gives something lighter than metal but very stiff and strong. Racing bikes, aeroplane wings and this Norqain watch case are all made of it.

A pocket watch is a watch on a chain that you carry in a pocket and lift out to read, the normal kind before wristwatches took over in the early 1900s. Royal Pop being a plastic pocket watch is a deliberate joke about an old-fashioned object. Its design copies a famous expensive wristwatch, the Royal Oak.

If the clock is ticking, time is running out and something must be done soon. It is a stock phrase about deadlines and pressure, used far beyond watches. Here the writer is making a pun, because this really is an industry of ticking clocks that is running out of time.

To part with something is to hand it over and give it up, usually unwillingly. Should you still wish to part with SFr14,000 means if you are still willing to pay that much. The phrase almost always suggests the thing is hard to let go of.

To be hit hard is to be badly damaged by something outside your control. Quartz watch sales were hit particularly hard by smart watches, meaning that part of the industry suffered more than the rest. You will meet the same phrase about towns hit hard by floods or shops hit hard by rising prices.

To account for a share of something is to make up that part of the total. Watches over SFr50,000 accounted for 37% of the value of exports means that expensive watches were 37% of all the money. The same phrase can also mean to explain something, so read it in context.

To be credited with something is to be widely given the praise for it. Swatch is credited with saving the industry in the 1980s, meaning people generally agree it deserves that praise. The phrase reports other people's opinion rather than stating a fact outright.

To hold your own is to do well enough against stronger opposition and not be pushed aside. Swatch's cheap plastic watches held their own against cheap Asian alternatives, so they kept their customers instead of losing them. It is praise for surviving a tough fight, not for winning it.

In rude health is a British phrase meaning strikingly strong and thriving, and rude here is an old sense meaning robust rather than impolite. The rude financial health of the very rich means wealthy buyers have plenty of money to spend. That is one reason the dearest watches sell best.

Down on a year earlier means lower than the same stretch of time twelve months before. Net profit was still down on a year earlier says that even after the Royal Pop rush, Swatch earned less than in the same half of the previous year. Business reports compare with a year earlier because seasons make month-to-month figures misleading.

King of the ring means the undisputed champion, and the ring is a boxing ring. Calling Rolex king of the ring says it is far ahead of every rival, with sales three times those of second-placed Cartier. The writer has also slipped in a pun, since a watch ring is part of the case.

Rolex is the biggest Swiss watchmaker and the most famous luxury watch brand in the world, founded in 1905. It sells about 1.2m watches a year at an average of SFr14,000 each, and buyers often have to join a waiting list. Unusually, it is owned by a charitable foundation rather than by shareholders or a family.

Patek Philippe is a Geneva watchmaker founded in 1839 and one of the most expensive brands in the world, known for very complicated hand-built mechanical watches. It is privately owned by one family. It is among the five brands taking most of the industry's money.

Cartier is a French jeweller, founded in Paris in 1847, that also makes watches, and it is the second-biggest seller of Swiss watches after Rolex. Unlike the other top brands it is not privately owned: it belongs to the listed group Richemont. Its sales are about a third of Rolex's.

Omega is a well-known Swiss watch brand, founded in 1848, that supplied the watches worn on the Moon landings. It is one of the five biggest sellers, but it belongs to the Swatch Group rather than being independent. It is the one big brand the article says has not been gaining share.

Audemars Piguet is a Swiss luxury watchmaker founded in 1875 by two families, Audemars and Piguet, whose descendants still own it. Its best-known watch is the Royal Oak, a steel sports watch from 1972 with an eight-sided face. In 2026 it lent that look to a cheap plastic Swatch called Royal Pop.

Swatch is a Swiss company that launched cheap, colourful plastic quartz watches in 1983 and is widely said to have saved Swiss watchmaking from Asian competition. The Swatch Group now owns Omega and several other brands and is the largest listed Swiss watchmaker. The move towards expensive watches has gone badly for it.

Norqain is a small Swiss watch firm started in 2018 and owned by the family that runs it, with watches selling for about SFr4,500 on average. The article uses it as proof that a new brand can still succeed, since it already sells up to 10,000 watches a year. Its chief executive, Ben Küffer, is the person quoted.

The Hans Wilsdorf Foundation is the charitable trust that owns Rolex, set up in 1945 by Hans Wilsdorf, the founder of Rolex, who had no children to leave it to. Because a foundation holds the shares, Rolex has no outside investors demanding bigger profits each year. The money instead goes into the watches and into causes around Geneva.
